questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It just had to be in Japan. You can't really know what it's like before you go...

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Ritsumeikan gave us a detailed pre-arrival guide.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A briefing a ritsumeikan university and a pamphlet that contained info on different arrival procedures.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Quite easy. I went for the private appartment (Free Pia). If you go to Freepia go for Freepia 1 (or 3), but 1 is cheaper.

People seemed to have a lot of fun in the dormitories (especially Tokiwa). I just chose a private appartment for private reasons. Also know that in dormitories you cant have people staying over late and some of them might divide boys and girls into different sections (not sure about this oen, but make sure to check before applying).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can walk to campus in about 25-30 mins from Freepia.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Freepia 1 and 2 are relatively cheap (around 35.000 yen a month)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register through an excel sheet. They explain it at the briefing as well as hand out papers that explain it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact the international center if in doubt.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try a CSC (Campus specific course) course or two. They are quite fun, and the work load is not too bad. Just keep in mind that they cost money and make sure you can get pre-approva (CSC is artsy stuff such as calligraphy, ikebana etc).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: IJL (Intensive Japanese Language Track) was quite intensive funnily enough, but nothing crazy. Just make sure not to register for English language classes that require a lot of preparation. That is why I suggest taking a CSC course or 2.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The IJL course has a lot more classes every week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
IJL lvl 5 =
Comphrehensive Japanese 5x a week
Listening and Speaking 2x a week
Writing 1x a week.

English Language courses:
12977:Introduction to Vernacular Culture (L)
11775:Lecture for Humanities (LC) § 11776:Selected Problems in Human

CSC courses: 
16598:Japanese Traditional Arts II (KF) - calligraphy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Calligraphy was fun to try and the work load is not too bad.
Same goes for Introduction to Vernacular Culture. And the subjects are quite interesting too.

IJL is quite hard, but you get to practice Japanese language every day. In addition I recommend going to BBP, where you can meet a lot of other exchange studetns as well as Japanese people. Here you can both practice Japanese as well as make new friends.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
None. I've been to Japan before :)
For people who haven't been before - you need to pay for national health insurance in Japan no matter what, so reconsider if you need your own travel insurance (I reckon you can do without).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was quite cheap in Freepia 1&2

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
BBP (Beyond Borders Plaza) is a nice hub, where you can meet people, exchange languages, participate in activities and such.

I thought about joining a football circle (club), but quite a few of them were private... Other circles  might be easier to join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: BBP hosts a lot of activites such as language exchanges events, social events etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Anything in BBP. its a good place to meet people and hang out.
Also Kyoto is a beautiful city, so take some time to explore it and see some of the temples /nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see some temples, go on a hike, go to a football game - something cultural :)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
BBP. 
Join a circle if you have a certain interest in sports, boardgames, dancing, whatever it might be, you can probably find likeminded people there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Sometimes Japanese people can be a bit hard to get close to.

Also the traffic can be a bit tricky sometimes, as the bikes ride on the sidewalk... and don't use a bell. Don't expect cars to stop for you.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are generally really nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Throw yourself out there (don't listen too much to advice, just do your own thing).

Even though you don't speak the language, don't let that hold you back too much. Most people are nice and accomodating. 

Go out and explore and see for yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: x

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finishing an intensive language track and meeting new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The studies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
